criteria.description: A single named module-level constant CLAIM_MAX_WORDS is defined in claims.py with the value 10_000.
criteria.verifyBy: Import claims and assert claims.CLAIM_MAX_WORDS == 10000; grep confirms it is a module-level constant defined once.

criteria.description: A typed, catchable rejection exception class (e.g. ClaimInputTooLong) is defined in claims.py, distinct from ClaimExtractionTruncated. It must be independently catchable: NOT a subclass of ClaimExtractionTruncated nor of ClaimParseError, so a caller can catch it specifically without also catching parse/truncation errors.
criteria.verifyBy: Assert the class exists in claims.py and is a subclass of Exception; assert issubclass(ClaimInputTooLong, ClaimExtractionTruncated) is False and issubclass(ClaimInputTooLong, ClaimParseError) is False; a test raises and catches it by its own type.

criteria.description: The word-count tripwire sits inside the single shared warm seam (generate_claims), positioned AFTER the cache-hit / source_hash freshness check but BEFORE the extraction/API call (extract_claims). All extraction entry points funnel through this seam, so both the (future) upload-triggered warm and the existing prepare/picker path are protected by the same check, and the trigger goes THROUGH the cache guard, not around it.
criteria.verifyBy: Test monkeypatches claims.extract_claims to record invocation; for an over-bound doc with NO fresh sidecar it asserts extraction was NEVER invoked (rejection precedes extraction). The behavioral guarantees in c4/c9/c10 (guard fires before extraction on every entry point) secure the shared-seam intent; implementation shape (e.g. whether the guard is textually a single line) is not independently graded.

criteria.description: A document whose text word count is strictly greater than CLAIM_MAX_WORDS AND which has no fresh valid sidecar for its current source_hash causes the warm seam to raise the typed rejection condition instead of proceeding to extraction.
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test feeds text with word count > CLAIM_MAX_WORDS (no cached sidecar) and asserts the typed rejection (e.g. ClaimInputTooLong) is raised via pytest.raises, with monkeypatched claims.extract_claims never invoked.

criteria.description: Idempotency invariant: a document that already has a fresh valid sidecar for its current source_hash returns the cached claims WITHOUT raising the bound rejection, EVEN IF its text is over CLAIM_MAX_WORDS words. The cache-hit path short-circuits before the tripwire.
criteria.verifyBy: Test primes a fresh valid sidecar (matching source_hash) for an over-bound doc, calls generate_claims, and asserts it returns the cached claims, does NOT raise ClaimInputTooLong, and does NOT invoke monkeypatched claims.extract_claims.

criteria.description: Boundary semantics are pinned: word_count > CLAIM_MAX_WORDS is rejected; word_count == CLAIM_MAX_WORDS proceeds to extraction (the limit value itself is allowed). Word count is computed as len(document_text.split()) — the same whitespace-splitting counting rule the guard itself uses; all boundary fixtures are built to that rule.
criteria.verifyBy: Two tests, fixtures counted by len(text.split()): a doc with exactly CLAIM_MAX_WORDS words proceeds to extraction (monkeypatched call invoked, no rejection); a doc with CLAIM_MAX_WORDS+1 words raises the typed rejection.

criteria.description: The rejection carries/produces a message that names the document's ACTUAL word count (computed via len(document_text.split()), a number distinct from the limit), the CLAIM_MAX_WORDS limit, and a suggestion to split or excerpt the document.
criteria.verifyBy: Test uses an over-bound fixture whose word count (len(text.split())) != 10000 (e.g. 10001); asserts str(exc) contains that actual word count as a number, contains 10000 (the limit), and contains split/excerpt guidance text — so a message echoing only the limit twice cannot pass.

criteria.description: Every rejection emits an app log line via the standard logging module (a module logger in claims.py, not a bare print), recording the document's actual word count (len(document_text.split())) as the correct integer. This log emission happens inside claims.py at the seam, before the exception propagates.
criteria.verifyBy: Test uses caplog to assert a log record is emitted by the claims module logger on rejection at INFO or WARNING level and that the record's message contains the exact actual word count of the input (an asserted integer equal to len(fixture_text.split())).

criteria.description: A document whose text word count is under (or equal to) CLAIM_MAX_WORDS and has no fresh sidecar proceeds to extraction normally (the tripwire does not block valid docs).
criteria.verifyBy: Pure-helper test with monkeypatched claims.extract_claims feeds under-bound text (len(text.split()) <= CLAIM_MAX_WORDS, no cached sidecar) and asserts the extraction call IS invoked and no rejection is raised — no live API call made.

criteria.description: The tripwire fires through the existing prepare/picker warm path, confirming the check protects that real path. The prepare path's background warm (_warm_claims) intentionally catches Exception and swallows the rejection (best-effort warm, per goal Part 1: extraction failure does not fail upload/warm) — so the typed condition is NOT required to propagate out of _warm_claims, and the prepare path must NOT surface an error (no 500) to the caller.
criteria.verifyBy: One test drives an over-bound doc (no fresh sidecar) through the real prepare/picker path with claims.extract_claims monkeypatched, and asserts: (a) claims.extract_claims is NEVER invoked; (b) the prepare path does not raise/500 to the caller (best-effort swallow → normal fire-and-forget response). The 'rejection log line fires' assertion is verified separately in c8 via caplog on the claims.py module-logger record emitted at the seam BEFORE propagation — c10 does NOT depend on _warm_claims's existing print (which caplog does not capture).

criteria.verifyBy: Endpoint test that spies the scheduling of the shared warm task (monkeypatch _warm_claims or capture BackgroundTasks.add_task): upload a FRESH doc (never warmed, under the bound), read document_id from the upload response body, and assert the shared warm task was scheduled exactly once with the uploading user's user_id and a doc_id equal to that returned document_id. No live API call is made. Code review confirms no separate bound pre-check exists in the handler ahead of scheduling.

criteria.description: The upload-triggered warm reuses the existing shared prepare/warm path (the same warm task the prepare endpoint schedules, which ultimately calls generate_claims); it introduces NO new claim-extraction/LLM implementation and no second LLM extraction call. criteria.description: Upload success is fully independent of extraction success: when the triggered warm/extraction raises (API error, tripwire, or any exception), the upload still returns the same success response it returns today and the file lands on disk.

criteria.description: After a failed/absent extraction, the doc remains loadable and behaves as an unwarmed doc (plain study mode) — no new failure mode.
criteria.verifyBy: Test with the warm/extraction raising: assert documents.load_document(user_id, doc_id) returns a non-None (title, text) tuple whose text equals the uploaded text for the uploading user, and claims.load_fresh_claims(user_id, doc_id, text) is None (no fresh sidecar) — matching an unwarmed doc's load semantics.

criteria.description: An already-warmed doc (valid/fresh claims sidecar for the current source_hash) is NOT re-extracted when the upload-triggered warm runs — idempotency is enforced solely by the existing generate_claims source_hash cache guard reached through the real shared warm path.
criteria.verifyBy: Test pre-seeds a fresh sidecar for the doc's current source_hash, then runs the upload-triggered warm end-to-end with the REAL load_fresh_claims/generate_claims cache guard live while spying the deeper LLM extraction step (extract_claims): assert the LLM extraction step is never invoked (short-circuited by source_hash freshness at the cache-hit branch) and the pre-seeded sidecar's content/mtime is unchanged.

criteria.description: An oversized doc's upload still succeeds (same success response as today) and lands a loadable file that behaves as unwarmed (no fresh sidecar); its warming is refused by the tripwire firing inside the shared warm seam, and the rejection reason — containing the doc's word count, the limit, and a split/excerpt suggestion — is surfaced to the uploading user. The upload does not gain a new failure mode from the oversized doc; the rejection is a message, not an upload error.
criteria.verifyBy: Test uploads a doc whose word count exceeds CLAIM_MAX_WORDS: assert the upload response returns the same success status as today with the file present and loadable as unwarmed (load_fresh_claims is None); assert the rejection reason surfaced to the user contains the doc's actual word count equal to len(uploaded_text.split()), the limit value, and a split/excerpt suggestion. Separately assert a doc under the bound is not rejected (no rejection message) and DOES schedule the shared warm task.

criteria.description: An oversized-doc rejection is logged with the doc's word count (an app log line is sufficient) as evidence for later tuning of the constant. The log originates from the existing typed+logged tripwire path in claims (reached through the shared warm seam), not from a duplicate handler-side check.
criteria.verifyBy: Test captures logs during an oversized upload and asserts a log record is emitted that includes the doc's word count (and ideally the limit), demonstrating the tripwire's typed+logged path was reached via the shared warm seam. No assertion is made about a redundant synchronous pre-check.

criteria.description: Idempotency proven through the full UPLOAD-COMPLETION end-to-end entry point (not merely a direct _warm_claims call): driving app.upload_document for a document that already has a fresh, valid extraction sidecar keyed by its current source_hash (uploading user's namespace) performs ZERO live extractions. The real generate_claims/load_fresh_claims source_hash freshness guard runs UNPATCHED and short-circuits; only the deeper live LLM decomposition step claims.extract_claims is spied and must record zero calls. The result must be shown NOT to be an artifact of in-flight de-dup: the exactly-one scheduled _warm_claims(user_id, doc_id) BackgroundTask is captured and run to completion exactly once, and the _claims_warming in-flight set is confirmed reset (empty) before the assertion.
criteria.verifyBy: TDD test in tests/test_upload_autowarm.py (run via `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_upload_autowarm.py -q`): seed a fresh valid sidecar keyed by the doc's current source_hash for the uploading user; spy ONLY claims.extract_claims leaving generate_claims/load_fresh_claims real; drive app.upload_document end-to-end; capture and execute exactly the one scheduled warm BackgroundTask to completion once; assert _claims_warming is empty, the extract_claims spy recorded zero calls, and the uploaded doc remains present and loadable.

criteria.description: The trigger routes THROUGH the single shared cache/freshness guard, proven behaviorally: with real generate_claims/load_fresh_claims intact and only claims.extract_claims spied, a fresh sidecar for the current source_hash yields ZERO extract_claims calls and a stale-or-absent sidecar yields EXACTLY ONE extract_claims call — demonstrating one source_hash freshness decision governs both outcomes.
criteria.verifyBy: TDD test in tests/test_upload_autowarm.py spying claims.extract_claims (generate_claims guard real): case (a) fresh sidecar for current source_hash -> zero extract_claims calls; case (b) stale or absent sidecar -> exactly one extract_claims call. In each case the scheduled warm task is captured and driven to completion exactly once and _claims_warming is confirmed reset so the count is deterministic. Runs under `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_upload_autowarm.py -q`.

criteria.verifyBy: TDD test in tests/test_upload_autowarm.py through the prepare/warm entry point spying claims.extract_claims (generate_claims guard real): unwarmed doc, scheduled warm task captured and run to completion exactly once -> exactly one extract_claims call; companion assertion that a fresh-sidecar doc through the same prepare path -> zero extract_claims calls (warm task, if scheduled, driven once and _claims_warming reset). criteria.description: Manually-placed _shared documents still get warmed via the prepare path exactly as before, and the upload auto-warm path preserves per-user namespace isolation. (a) An unwarmed _shared doc driven through the prepare path triggers live extraction once resolving against the _shared namespace. (b) Namespace isolation on the upload path, proven via the ORGANIC invariant rather than a contrived doc_id collision: because save_upload writes the file into the uploading user's own directory (user_dir(user_id)) and generate_claims resolves namespace user-first-then-_shared, an uploaded doc always warms in the UPLOADER's namespace — assert the executed warm targets the uploader's user_id and that the per-user sidecar is the one written/extracted, while a pre-existing _shared sidecar at the same doc_id (seeded by the fixture as the isolation control) is neither read nor written and is not the target of extraction. If a doc_id collision is exercised, the fixture must explicitly force the uploaded doc_id (e.g. monkeypatching the uuid source in save_upload) and the criterion is that isolation holds regardless — the _shared sidecar stays untouched.
criteria.verifyBy: TDD test in tests/test_upload_autowarm.py using the _shared fixtures/patterns from the existing mirror tests, spying claims.extract_claims (generate_claims guard real): (a) place an unwarmed _shared doc, drive the prepare path, run the scheduled warm to completion exactly once, assert exactly one extract_claims call resolving against the _shared namespace; (b) seed a _shared sidecar at a chosen doc_id as an isolation control, then upload a doc as a normal user (forcing the same doc_id via the fixture if a collision is being exercised), assert the executed warm targets the uploader's user_id namespace, that the per-user sidecar is written/extracted, and that the _shared sidecar is neither read nor written nor extracted. Runs under `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_upload_autowarm.py -q`.
